Probe on a sandbox HOME, with reconcile --mode apply --entry-point installer for hosts claude, codex, cursor and opencode. With an install-only grant for all tools, the HOME snapshot diff was empty (no host config written); calls were only uv tool install, graphify update and version probes. With a wire-only grant (CLIs removed), no npm, uv, pipx or brew ran, and the result reports failures install_not_consented. Mutation M1 (receipts.sh rtk wire -> no capability) makes test-rt-hooks-batch fail, and M5 (graphify platform wire guard removed) makes test-rt-graphify-agentmemory fail. Separate Pi issue below (major).

Cursor-only. Global rules are now installed per tool when that tool has wire consent, and optimize-five no longer passes --global. Separate residual, also moot: install-recommended-tools-cursor still deploys ~/.cursor/hooks/toolstack/* without consent (minor issue below).

is_legacy_routing_hook removes lean-ctx deny, redirect and rewrite only when RT_PATCH_LEANCTX=1 and RTK replaces them. Mutation M2 (leanctx_owned=True) makes test-reconcile-recommended-tools fail ('patch-hooks keeps LeanCTX's own hooks without LeanCTX consent').

Exported in all eight entry scripts, and the test checks that the export comes before any source. R6-07 probe: codex config.toml had [mcp_servers.lean-ctx.env] MY_API_KEY=secret123; I ran optimize-five-tool-stack --host codex with full consent. config.toml.sb-backup is byte-identical to the original, and MY_API_KEY moved into leanctx.env. A second run left config.toml unchanged.

Reclaim is serialised by a guard directory and staleness is re-checked under it. Stress probe: 25 trials of 8 concurrent waiters on a dead-pid lock gave total_overlap=0 and total_timeout=0. Mutation M6 (re-check removed) fails 'a lock that is no longer stale survives a late reclaim'. The unit tests simulate the interleavings deterministically; there is no true concurrent test, which is acceptable.

Partial, per the decision. The LeanCTX cargo hint is now 'cargo install lean-ctx --version <template min_version> --locked'. The RTK hint names >= 0.42.0 (brew cannot pin). Other packages have no template min_version.

sb-optimize-stack.sh and sb-verify-synergy.sh exit 2 when run from the plugin root, with an explicit --project-root, through a symlinked path, or with a trailing /. SB_ALLOW_PLUGIN_ROOT=1 allows it (rc 0). A subdirectory of the plugin root is not refused, which is low risk. A correct inverse mutation makes test-sb-optimize-stack-modes and test-sb-small-scripts fail.

Without Context Mode wire consent the script prints SKIP and leaves the file untouched. With consent it writes atomically, keeps mode 640, and leaves the original in .sb-backup; a re-run keeps that backup. Mutation M3 makes test-install-recommended-tools-hosts fail. Note: write_atomic follows symlinks by the sb_host_config (H2) contract. A symlinked ~/.codex/AGENTS.md has its target replaced, with the backup beside the target. So the orchestrator's 'no symlink following' expectation is not met literally: accept it as the H2 contract or decide otherwise.
Base 9b5db30 merged as 62dc496, and commit messages now carry red/green evidence. The base has since moved (94800f8); see the stale-base minor issue.

issues.problem: Regression on Pi in honest flows with consent. R1 (7348fe7) changed install-pi.py so that no --enable-tool means 'enable nothing' (at base it meant enable all). Several callers still invoke it without --enable-tool, so a user who granted wire consent ends up with every Pi server disabled: optimize_context_mode_pi, the graphify pre:pi platform command in stack-optimizer.sh, and the recommended-tools.sh registry command. optimize_rtk_pi meanwhile prints 'OK: Pi RTK is wired by the shared native tool_call adapter', but nothing ever enables rtk. Only the reconciler batch and install-leanctx-sb pass --enable-tool. The flows test only asserts that 'install-pi --repo-root' was invoked, so the regression is not caught.
issues.evidence: Probe 1, fresh HOME: sb-consent grant rtk and context_mode --all-projects (install, wire, enforce), then bash scripts/optimize-rtk-context-mode.sh --host pi --project-root <proj> --skip-cm-doctor gives rc=0, and ~/.pi/agent/extensions/silver-bullet-five-tool-stack/config.json .servers = {graphify:false, agentmemory:false, context_mode:false, leanctx:false, rtk:false}. Probe 2: grant graphify and agentmemory, then sb-optimize-stack.sh --apply --host pi gives the same config, with every server disabled. git show 02eff38:install-pi.py:111 has 'requested = set(all_tools) if enabled_tools is None'.
issues.suggested_fix: Pass --enable-tool for each consented tool at every caller: context_mode, plus rtk in optimize_rtk_pi when WIRE_RTK=1; graphify, and agentmemory when consented, in the stack-optimizer pre:pi and recommended-tools pi commands. Better, make one helper build the args from sb_consent_granted TOOL wire. Add flow tests that assert the resulting config.json enables the consented tools and not the others.

issues.problem: With no consent at all, --host pi still writes the user's ~/.pi/agent/settings.json (adds the SB extension) and installs the extension, config.json and manifest. The same script gates the codex and opencode AGENTS.md writes on wire consent, so host-config writes here are not consistently consent-gated.
issues.evidence: Fresh HOME, no consent: bash scripts/install-recommended-tools-global.sh --host pi gives rc=0 and creates .pi/agent/settings.json {extensions:[~/.pi/agent/extensions/silver-bullet-five-tool-stack]}, plus the extension index.ts and config.json, and .local/state/five-tool-stack/manifest.json.
issues.suggested_fix: Skip with a consent hint unless at least one tool has wire consent, as install_agents_file does.

issues.problem: optimize-five-tool-stack.sh --force with no consent, on a cursor host or --host all, runs install-recommended-tools-cursor.sh. That calls rt_installer_post_install without any consent check, which deploys about 45 files into ~/.cursor/hooks/toolstack and writes ~/.cursor/state/toolstack/repo-root. This is Cursor-only, so it becomes moot once Cursor removal deletes this path. Make sure the removal does delete it.
issues.evidence: HOME3, no consent: optimize-five-tool-stack.sh --host all --project-root <proj> --force; the HOME diff shows +45 files under .cursor/hooks/toolstack/ and .cursor/state/toolstack/repo-root.
issues.suggested_fix: Handled by the Cursor removal (HC). Otherwise, gate post_install on rt_any_five_tool_mutation_allowed with wire.

issues.problem: Merge conflict with the current fix/H4a-toolgates-consent (3e250ef): both branches removed the normalize fallback, H4a with "${path:-.}". H4b's comment ('target paths are never empty') does not hold for a direct file_path that contains a blank line (printf '%s\n' "$direct" emits an empty line). The normaliser then fails, and set -e plus the ERR trap exit the whole gate 0, allowing the call. This is an opt-in gate only.
issues.evidence: git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD fix/H4a-toolgates-consent: CONFLICT (content) in hooks/alumnium-gate.sh. The merge with claude/optimistic-ramanujan-tccfud is clean.
issues.suggested_fix: When H4a lands, resolve by taking H4a's ${path:-.} version.

issues.problem: The reconciler reports success actions (optimize_rtk_context_mode, install_leanctx_sb) and restart_required=true even when the child script skipped everything for lack of wire consent. Install-only users get a misleading report and a reload prompt. This is probably pre-existing.
issues.evidence: Install-only grant, reconcile apply --host claude: components rtk/context_mode actions ['optimize_rtk_context_mode'], leanctx actions ['install_leanctx_sb'], top-level restart_required true; stderr shows 'SKIP: ... no consent'. The HOME diff is empty.
issues.suggested_fix: Call the child only when rt_mutation_allowed TOOL wire, otherwise report a 'wire_not_consented' failure, as the install path does.

issues.location: hooks/lib/stack-optimizer.sh:160-172 (pre-existing; owned by H4a, not H4b)
issues.problem: The agentmemory .env merge is not idempotent. Every apply run adds a blank line before the managed block and overwrites .env.bak, so the user's original .env backup is lost after the second run.
issues.evidence: Three runs of sb-optimize-stack.sh --apply give ~/.agentmemory/.env with 11, then 12, then 13 lines; the diff against .env.bak is one extra blank line each time. The same code is at base 02eff38.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip trailing blank lines before appending, or skip the write when the content is unchanged; keep the first backup per run (sb_host_config).

validation.tests: Mutation checks in a git-archive copy: M1, M2, M3, M5, M6 and a corrected M4 each made their tests fail (meaningful tests). The scoped coverage run reported 8004 passed and 5 failed. Four of the failures (test-install-codex, test-install-cursor, test-install-cursor-archive, test-install-global-toolstack) were ENOSPC: the shared disk filled up, 'No space left on device' and 'sb-consent: could not update'. The fifth (test-no-pipe-into-grep-quiet) is the stale-base issue.

Python 1880/1880 statements and 820/820 branches; JS 220/220 lines; Bash 31 of 32 files at 100%. Gaps came from ENOSPC and from my test selection. install-global-toolstack.sh (its test hit ENOSPC) and receipts.sh 555-591 (its tests test-rt-convergence-* were missing from my selection) reached 100% in a small supplementary run, so receipts.sh is at 100% only across both runs. hooks/alumnium-gate.sh:37 was missed in both runs; it is covered by tests/hooks/test-opt-in-gates-hostile-config.sh ('a shell call without a command'), which I did not select, so I found no real gap.
